question: Measure phi, the share of DAF labour and outsourced-administration cost spent handling the 15 sponsor-side processes (exceptions, reviews, service contacts), at two or more sponsors including one community foundation with $250m-1bn of DAF assets, using time studies, functional-expense notes in audited statements, or administrator service agreements
conclusion_affected: AI-economics v2 pool size; vendor platform break-even; 'AI pays only at national scale'
rationale: phi is the largest unsourced multiplier left after anchoring to Part IX. Moving phi from its bottom to its top tercile raises the share of NAT_LARGE (process, draw) pairs where some intervention pays from 0.49 to 0.69. v1's own pool implies phi of 0.07 at Fidelity and 0.15 at DAFgiving360, so v1 does not settle it either

question: Measure redesign elimination shares d and counterparty adoption for P06 (per-grant eligibility re-checks), P09/P10 (share of grants still paid by cheque, reissue and escheat rates) and P16 (recipient attribution) at any sponsor or processor, so that redesign is tested against data rather than assumed
conclusion_affected: AI-economics v2 ranking: D first on gross in 11 of 16 processes
rationale: Of all parameters, d moves the gross ranking most. The share of (process, draw) pairs where D ranks first by gross rises from 0.36 to 0.81 between the bottom and top tercile of d, and B's share falls from 0.47 to 0.15. Every d value in v1 and v2 is still an assumption

question: Run, or find a published, controlled benchmark of AI-assisted handling for P03 (complex-asset intake), P07 (non-standard grantee due diligence) and P11 (service contacts) that measures time saved (s), the share of cases the model can handle (a) and the reviewer override and re-review rate (q). Use the A/B/C design in the Ren/RCF audit
conclusion_affected: AI-economics v2: 'C rarely ranks first'; whether AI per-process cases ever pay
rationale: In P03 and P07 the probability that C ranks first by gross rises from about 0.02 to about 0.33 between the bottom and top tercile of either a or s. These are the only processes where measured AI performance could change the ranking. In 8 processes P(C first) stays below 0.01 in every tercile of a, s or d

question: Price a shared DAF AI platform from vendor and administrator disclosures (Ren, TIFIN Give, Foundation Source/Vennfi, Blackbaud, Benevity pricing pages, contracts in 990 Schedule O or Part VII-B, public RFPs): annual platform cost, per-sponsor integration and support cost, and the share of savings vendors capture as fees
conclusion_affected: Entrant strategy: vendor or network-scale AI; platform break-even sponsor count
rationale: Break-even needs about 8 large-national-equivalents (p50, with only 5 such sponsors existing), about 59 mid-national or $1bn community-foundation equivalents, or about 236 $250m community foundations. All three numbers rest on the assumed platform cost ($1.5-6m a year), per-sponsor cost ($10-100k) and fee share (0.2-0.5)

question: Establish whether the process labour at the largest nationals sits with their affiliated administrators (Fidelity's $139.7m line 11a; Schwab and Vanguard affiliates), and whether those administrators already run AI on grant review or donor service. The large-national archetype is the only one where a self-built platform pays in more than 10% of draws
conclusion_affected: Entrant strategy: who buys DAF AI (sponsor, administrator or vendor)
rationale: P(self-built platform pays) is 0.20 at NAT_LARGE and 0.00 for every other archetype. The network break-even on the observed FY2024 population is reachable in 43% of draws when the giants are included, 26% without them, and 0.4% for community foundations under $250m alone. Whoever controls the giants' administration controls the AI economics

question: Anchor P16 (nonprofit-side DAF gift attribution) to observed recipient cost: gift-processing staff cost from nonprofit 990s, Chariot or Blackbaud pricing, or survey data. v2 still scales this pool linearly from v1 assumptions
conclusion_affected: AI-economics: P16 'largely should not exist'; sector-side value of a remittance standard
rationale: P16 is the only process with no observed cost anchor in v2. Its pool ($2.2m p50 at NAT_LARGE volumes) is the second-largest in the large-national archetype and drives the sector-standard argument
